policy: Post-hoc strict v2; all five components jointly required. Valid alternatives receive quality credit independently. Candidate and v1 bytes preserved.

source.title: F1-ATPase is a highly efficient molecular motor that rotates with discrete 120 degree steps

reviews.reason: Question/mechanism/intervention/readouts include stepping, ATP/load discrimination, drag-derived work and condition-specific chemical free energy. However, the joint positive conclusion assigns one ATP per 120-degree step from bulk rate matching with unknown active fraction and ATP-dependent waiting. Its own caveat concedes stoichiometry is assumed. That critical coupling-to-efficiency inference prevents a qualified predicted-outcome hit; merely naming 120 degrees does not rescue it.

The stepping/ATP/load question and intervention align, but no ATP/ADP/phosphate free-energy estimate or supported work-per-turnover comparison is made. The primary histogram null and one-ATP-per-step assignment are also non-identifying. Thus joint historical readout and prediction fail despite naming 120 degrees.

Question, stepping mechanism and ATP/load intervention match. Work/chemical-free-energy energetics are explicitly deferred, and one turnover per step is inferred rather than validated. Consequently the joint historical readout and qualified prediction fail.

Step question/mechanism and ATP/load intervention align. There is no torque-angle work and actual hydrolysis-free-energy comparison, and bulk-turnover attribution is not resolved. The full historical readout/prediction is therefore missing; no requirement to guess 120 degrees was imposed.

The mechanical question and ATP/load manipulation align, but neither calibrated work/chemical free energy nor credible chemical coupling is measured. Step-finder output alone lacks independent validation; complete historical readout/prediction does not qualify.

Step/coupling question and ATP/load manipulation match. No actual chemical-free-energy comparison is made; angular periodicity and rate dependencies also cannot establish the asserted 1:1 nucleotide event. Joint historical energetic readout and qualified prediction are missing.

Question, stepping mechanism and ATP-by-load intervention match the mechanochemical part. The proposal explicitly leaves torque/work/efficiency unmeasured: no torque-angle work calculation or ATP/ADP/phosphate free-energy comparison supports the historical energetic result. Thus the joint stepping-plus-energetics readout and prediction are incomplete; not assuming a 120-degree answer is good practice and is NOT the reason for the miss.

Question, stepping mechanism and ATP-by-load intervention match the mechanochemical part. The proposal explicitly leaves torque/work/efficiency unmeasured: no torque-angle work calculation or ATP/ADP/phosphate free-energy comparison supports the historical energetic result. Thus the joint stepping-plus-energetics readout and prediction are incomplete; not assuming a 120-degree answer is good practice and is NOT the reason for the miss.

Question, stepping mechanism and ATP-by-load intervention match the mechanochemical part. The proposal explicitly leaves torque/work/efficiency unmeasured: no torque-angle work calculation or ATP/ADP/phosphate free-energy comparison supports the historical energetic result. Thus the joint stepping-plus-energetics readout and prediction are incomplete; not assuming a 120-degree answer is good practice and is NOT the reason for the miss.

Question, stepping/coupling mechanism and ATP/load intervention align. The proposal explicitly forbids converting torque to efficiency and supplies no actual ATP/ADP/phosphate free-energy or work-per-step comparison. Thus the joint historical energetic readout/prediction is incomplete; a valid narrower program still receives scientific-quality credit.

The proposal supplies stepping/coupling question and mechanism, ATP/load interventions with credible angular/chemical controls, measured steps and conditional torque-clamp work using actual ATP/ADP/phosphate free energy, and a conditional three-step/three-turnover outcome. The explicit efficiency-calculation gate prevents unsupported energy claims. This matches the historical stepping-plus-energetics direction without requiring the candidate to assert an unobserved exact efficiency or 120-degree answer in advance.

Question, stepping mechanism and ATP/load intervention align. Torque and power are conditional, but no torque-angle work versus actual ATP/ADP/phosphate chemical-free-energy experiment or its supported energetic prediction is supplied. Thus the joint historical readout/prediction is incomplete, independently of the exact step angle.
